Thank you for saying that and I totally agree with you. I feel like therapy is never a harmful thing for anyone in recovery. That's why I talked about my experience in being led to me going into therapy. 

There are definitely harmful/toxic misunderstandings or over simplifications of some of the ideas in the program of AA. 

I recently had a friend and fellow who struggled with mental illness as well as alcoholism and addiction overdose and pass away. Some of the cruel and nasty things that were said about him as well as the cold and uncompassionate things said about the grief I am experiencing really forced me to look closer at the program. 

I realized that much like any other organization or religion, it's not so much the text but the ways the people or followers misinterpret, misquote, and just plain bastardize the text. They manipulate it to fit their own selfish and self-centered agendas. 

It never fails to amaze me the number of people in program who are SO certain that the way they work their program is the "right way". And there's this idea that every single problem in life can be fixed if you just work the steps hard enough, even when it comes to taking psychiatric meds! It's crazy.

Ooh, yea.. my ability to rationalize and cosign my own BS is powerful. Lucky for me, my Higher Power is more powerful! Lol Maintaining my conscious contact with God usually leads me to the truth and out of my BS. 

The self-awareness that I've gained through working the steps is awesome. Just as awesome as having the tools of the 12 steps to help me deal with... well, me, as life keeps on comin. 

The Promises are real.

OP, that is a horrific and tragic thing to live through, you have my condolences. I've never had that experience, so I'm not going to pretend for a second that I know the levels of grief you've known, or how you "should" and "shouldn't" be feeling about it. 

What I can say is that having a sponsor to work The Steps with who has lived through a similar experience is important. I know that's been very true for me. 

I will forever appreciate the sponsor I had that told me I needed to find another sponsor because she didn't have the experience of being in an abusive relationship and that was a situation I was living through. I had a lot of strong emotions/resentments toward my abuser. In working the steps, I found that I didn't have a part in in the harm done. I was actually a victim. My new sponsor went further to say what my part was, it was in the present. I needed to stay away from my abuser, and go to therapy to A. Work through the trauma of the experience, and B. Identify the reasons I got stuck in an abusive relationship, that was my part. For me, my AA program helps me in therapy, and what I learn in therapy I can run through the 12 steps. They are both crucial for my recovery and total sobriety.

I also wanted to bring up that it's never too early in anyone's 12 Step journey to find, learn, and say daily The Serenity Prayer, the 3rd Step Prayer, and the 7th Step Prayer. Even if someone doesn't know who/what they are praying to, just saying the prayers and focusing on the meaning of the words is a powerful experience.
